title: Optimal Diffractive Focusing of Vortex Beams
authors: Roohollah Ghobadi, Carrie Rodriguez, Lukas Scarfe, Maxim A. Efremov, Ebrahim Karimi
abstract: We formulate diffractive ring focusing of paraxial beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) through a finite circular aperture as a variational optimization problem. For a fixed topological charge, we determine the real-valued radial pupil that maximizes the intensity at a prescribed ring radius and propagation distance under a normalization constraint on the input field. The resulting problem admits an exact analytical solution: the optimal pupil combines the familiar Fresnel phase structure with an OAM-dependent Bessel radial modulation, and the associated eigenvalue yields a rigorous upper bound on the achievable ring intensity. We further analyze the lens-assisted configuration and derive a simple bound that allows direct comparison between diffractive and refractive vortex focusing. The theory also provides a quantitative framework for evaluating the performance of practical mask designs, including binary Fresnel-Bessel zone plates and amplitude-weighted pupils. We have experimentally tested our predictions in the optical domain by implementing the corresponding vortex beam pupils and comparing their propagation and focusing performance with the optimal solution. Our results establish the vortex-beam analogue of optimal amplitude-only focusing and identify the fundamental limits governing diffractive concentration of structured waves
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to find the optimal pupil function for maximizing the intensity of vortex beams (carrying OAM) focused onto a ring. By solving a variational eigenvalue problem, the authors derive the optimal pupil structure, which combines Fresnel and Bessel modulations. They validate these theoretical limits through both detailed analysis and experimental implementation using SLMs.
main_problem: The paper addresses the optimization problem of achieving the maximum possible intensity concentration when focusing paraxial beams carrying Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) through a finite circular aperture.
main_result: The optimal pupil profile combines Fresnel phase structure with an OAM-dependent Bessel radial modulation, establishing a rigorous upper bound on achievable ring intensity for structured waves.
method: The problem is formulated as a variational optimization problem leading to an integral-kernel eigenvalue problem, which is solved analytically.
model_or_system: The system involves paraxial beams with OAM ($\ell$) propagating through a circular aperture. The analysis is conducted in the paraxial wave regime, modeling the focusing objective as maximizing intensity at a specific ring radius.
key_observables: Maximum achievable ring intensity ($\Lambda(\ell)$), optimal pupil function ($\psi^+_\ell$), and focusing efficiency ($\eta_\ell(\psi)$).
important_parameters: Topological charge ($\ell$), aperture radius ($R$), target ring radius ($ho^*$), and propagation distance ($	au_f$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the paraxial approximation and assumes the input field is aperture-limited.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the OAM dependence of the optimal eigenfunction and relative focusing strength, and compare experimental peak focal ring intensities for various mask types across different OAM orders.
paper_structure: The paper first formulates the optimal focusing problem variationally, deriving the optimal pupil structure. It then compares this theoretical optimum against practical mask designs (binary vs. amplitude-weighted) and experimentally tests these predictions.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental, analytically derived upper bound for energy concentration in structured light beams, which has direct implications for designing high-performance optical elements and understanding wave propagation limits.
